title: Molecular Dynamics and Energetic Insights into Novel PARP15 Inhibitors: A Structural Approach for Targeting BRCA-Mutated Breast Cancer.
authors: Alotaibi, Badriyah Shadid; Dwivedi, Vivek Dhar; Kamal, Mohammad Amjad
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选PARP15小分子抑制剂，对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法虽含物理模拟但与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer remains a critical global health issue, particularly in patients with BRCA1/2 mutations, which lead to genomic instability and increased cancer susceptibility. While PARP inhibitors targeting PARP1 and PARP2 have shown clinical success through synthetic lethality, PARP15, a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase involved in DNA repair and tumour progression, remains largely understudied. METHODS: A structure-based virtual screening approach was applied to identify potential PARP15 inhibitors. The screening was performed on a Bioactive Screening Compound Library consisting of over 12,200 druglike small molecules. Using the MTiOpenScreen platform, 1,500 candidate compounds were initially shortlisted. Molecular docking was then conducted to identify top-binding compounds, followed by 500- nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations to assess complex stability. Principal component analysis (PCA), free energy landscape (FEL) evaluation, and absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiling were also performed to characterise compound behaviour and drug-likeness. RESULTS: Three compounds, F2002-0551, F2028-0309, and F1495-1822, emerged with docking scores surpassing the known PARP15 inhibitor, Niraparib. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed their structural stability with low RMSD values and favourable FELs. PCA revealed consistent ligand dynamics, and ADME analysis showed high gastrointestinal absorption and other drug-like characteristics. Superimposition analysis demonstrated minimal deviation in docked poses, indicating strong and stable interactions with PARP15. DISCUSSION: These results highlight the therapeutic potential of the selected compounds as novel PARP15 inhibitors. Their favourable binding stability and pharmacokinetic profiles support their candidacy for further development against BRCA-mutated breast cancer. CONCLUSION: F2002-0551, F2028-0309, and F1495-1822 represent promising leads for PARP15 inhibition. This study offers a computational foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic exploration in BRCA-associated breast cancer.
abstract_zh: 引言：乳腺癌仍然是一个关键的全球健康问题，尤其是在携带BRCA1/2突变的患者中，这些突变导致基因组不稳定并增加癌症易感性。虽然靶向PARP1和PARP2的PARP抑制剂通过合成致死机制在临床上取得了成功，但PARP15——一种参与DNA修复和肿瘤进展的单ADP-核糖转移酶——在很大程度上仍未得到充分研究。方法：采用基于结构的虚拟筛选方法来识别潜在的PARP15抑制剂。筛选在包含超过12,200个类药小分子的生物活性筛选化合物库中进行。利用MTiOpenScreen平台，初步筛选出1,500个候选化合物。随后进行分子对接以识别最佳结合化合物，并进行了500纳秒的分子动力学模拟以评估复合物稳定性。还进行了主成分分析（PCA）、自由能景观（FEL）评估以及吸收、分布、代谢和排泄（ADME）分析，以表征化合物行为和类药性。结果：三个化合物F2002-0551、F2028-0309和F1495-1822脱颖而出，其对接分数超过了已知的PARP15抑制剂Niraparib。分子动力学模拟通过低RMSD值和有利的FEL确认了它们的结构稳定性。PCA揭示了一致的配体动力学，ADME分析显示高胃肠吸收和其他类药特性。叠加分析显示对接姿态偏差极小，表明与PARP15存在强且稳定的相互作用。讨论：这些结果突显了所选化合物作为新型PARP15抑制剂的治疗潜力。它们有利的结合稳定性和药代动力学特征支持其作为针对BRCA突变乳腺癌进一步开发的候选药物。结论：F2002-0551、F2028-0309和F1495-1822代表了PARP15抑制的有前景的先导化合物。本研究为BRCA相关乳腺癌的未来实验验证和治疗探索提供了计算基础。
